The release where Atrium learns to run more than one account, tells you when an agent needs you, and lets you take a kill back — plus a first run that gets you to your first agent without opening the README, and a rebuilt settings panel for everything after.

## Breaking

- **On modern terminals, `ctrl-m`/`ctrl-i`/`ctrl-h`/`ctrl-[` are no longer the same keys as `enter`/`tab`/`backspace`/`esc`.** Atrium moved to Bubble Tea v2, which always asks the terminal to disambiguate them; on Ghostty, Kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, foot, iTerm2, Rio and modifyOtherKeys-capable xterms they now arrive as distinct keys. No Atrium binding relied on the old conflation, so nothing you press today changes meaning — but if you drive Atrium from a script or macro that sends `ctrl-m` to mean Enter, send Enter. Esc is instant now, too: it no longer waits out an escape-sequence timeout.

## Highlights

- **Guided first run.** A new install walks you through picking an agent, detects which CLIs are actually on your PATH, and hands you a board with one clear next step — instead of a blank screen and a README.
- **Multiple Claude and GitHub accounts, managed in-app.** Add accounts, see which login each one is *really* signed in as, group the session list by account, and route each worktree's `gh` to its own credentials. Account pools rotate work across available logins, and Atrium refuses to launch a session onto the wrong Claude login rather than quietly billing it.
- **You get told when an agent needs you.** A bell, an OSC 9 notification that survives SSH, or a desktop notification when a background session finishes a turn or blocks on a prompt. Notifications stay quiet while you're looking at Atrium, a blocked session outranks a finished one, and any session can be muted.
- **A kill you can take back.** `ctrl-x` used to be the one unrecoverable action — worktree removed, branch force-deleted. It's now undoable, and Atrium warns first about commits a delete would actually discard.
- **Command palette.** `ctrl-k` finds any action by name and runs it. Actions the current selection can't take are dimmed with the reason, so the palette explains itself instead of just failing.
- **A real settings panel.** Two panes, ten categories, search, per-setting reset and deep links — with agent profiles editable without leaving the app. Most settings apply live.
- **The board bends to the task.** Layout presets on `\`, a draggable divider with finer width steps, project section headers, reorderable sessions and account clusters, and new filter predicates: `effort:`, `model:`, `mode:`, `account:`, `note:`, `pr:`, plus bare `muted` and `unread`.
- **Prompts queue instead of getting lost.** Queued prompts are a persisted FIFO with delivery acks and an overlay to review or cancel them, submitted prompts are kept for reuse, and a new-session draft you escaped out of survives a restart.
- **Comment on a diff line.** Annotate a line or a range in the diff tab and queue it straight to the agent.
- **Fan one prompt across profiles.** N-variant spawn starts the same prompt on several agents at once, so you can compare what comes back.
- **Atrium shows up in your terminal's chrome.** The window title and taskbar carry the fleet's state, copies reach your clipboard over SSH via OSC 52, branch and PR text is clickable via OSC 8, and the hint bar is clickable — with an off-switch for mouse capture when you'd rather your terminal keep its own selection.
- **A programmable surface.** `atrium ls --json`, `atrium peek` and `atrium send` let another agent — or a script — drive the board.
- **Sharper status.** Atrium tells an agent waiting on a sub-agent apart from one that's done, holds "working" from a version-independent hook heartbeat, and keeps a bounded history of every status transition.
- **A command log.** Every tmux, git and gh command Atrium runs is recorded and viewable, so a surprising outcome leaves a trail.
- **An empty board worth looking at.** Five generative splash patterns — rain, tunnel, ripple, galaxy, aurora — rotating per launch, a full-window screensaver, and an off switch.

## Fixes

- **Prompts land.** New-session and queued prompts go through a verified, closed-loop send that confirms the text arrived and submitted — including long multi-line prompts Claude collapses into a paste chip, and prompts sitting behind a trust or setup screen, which are now surfaced instead of silently stalling.
- **Sessions survive the edges.** In-flight sessions are no longer orphaned by a signal shutdown or a force-quit, zombie tmux clients are reaped, lost sessions recover safely and visibly, and a second Atrium on the same data dir is refused rather than left to clobber the first.
- **Attach and detach behave.** Returning from an attach refreshes the whole list immediately, a tmux client exiting mid-attach returns you to the TUI, raw-mode failures are surfaced rather than leaving detach mysteriously broken, and prompt delivery and auto-accept keep running while you're attached.
- **Auto-accept stops guessing wrong.** It no longer Enter-approves Claude selection menus, Codex and Gemini quoted literals, or anything but the confirmation shapes it actually recognizes.
- **Agent detection keeps up with Claude.** Busy, permission-dialog, trust-gate and footer detection are re-anchored to markers that survive Claude's reflows and rewordings, and keyed on the halves you can't rebind.
- **The UI stops shearing.** The paused view wraps instead of tearing, notices no longer reflow the layout in clean mode, the hint bar gets its row back when a modal closes, long descriptions wrap instead of clipping, the create form fits an 80-column terminal, and glyphs render on plain fonts without a Nerd Font.
- **Sessions start where they should.** Window names are sanitized for tmux 3.7, gitignored paths can be symlinked into worktrees via `link_paths`, a resumed session with no conversation starts blank, and a new session's cursor isn't stolen when its async start completes.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZviBaratz/atrium/main/install.sh | bash
```

Or with Go — note this builds from source and reports a `dev` version (the
script installs the version-stamped, self-updating release binary):

```bash
go install github.com/ZviBaratz/atrium@v0.9.0
```

This is a 0.x release — APIs and behavior may change.
